sourceEvidence.claim: BLOCK 2, Type I main text — 'α is the probability of making a type I error (usually 0.05 is chosen). kypExtensions.summary: The verdict-×-reality reading grammar of the printed grid: every error question decomposes into MOVE 1 what did the study conclude (reject / not reject H0 — the rows), MOVE 2 what is reality (H1 an effect exists / H0 none exists — the columns), MOVE 3 cross them to name the cell (Power (1 – β) / Type I error (α) / Type II error (β) / the silent correct cell), MOVE 4 pull the right lever, MOVE 5 separate statistical from clinical significance; plus the 'two ways to be right, two ways to be wrong' frame and the observation that the two printed Correct-result sentences ARE the two blue cells (the print's layout, the pairing is KYP's reading).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the grid and the definitions but never states the cross-reading procedure nor the blue-cell/Correct-result pairing; the grammar is KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] reality-by-decision + blocks[3] the steps block + the registry visual's Zone A rule strip

kypExtensions.summary: The courtroom frame for the two errors (the null hypothesis as defendant): Type I error (α) = convicting an innocent defendant — rejecting an H0 that is true (false positive); Type II error (β) = acquitting a guilty one — failing to reject an H0 that is false (the real effect walks free); packaged as the KYP mnemonic 'α ACCUSES THE INNOCENT NULL; β ACQUITS THE TRUE EFFECT'.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the definitions and its own cry-wolf anchors; the courtroom personification and the α-accuses/β-acquits code are KYP's design (the cry-wolf pair remains attributed to the source).
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics[2] + blocks[2] the decoder list + usmle.pivots[0]

kypExtensions.summary: The four-lever design reading of '↑ power and ↓ β by:': n–E–P–α in printed order (sample size, expected Effect size, Precision, α level), with the split the page implies but does not state — levers 1–3 raise power without spending Type I safety, lever 4 buys power with α on the printed see-saw ('Generally, when type I error increases, type II error decreases.'), and power as a design quantity computed before the data exist (why the page prints a lever list rather than a formula).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the four levers and the see-saw sentence as parallel facts; the free-vs-traded lever split, the n–E–P–α code, and the design-quantity framing are KYP's organization.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] power-levers + blocks[3] the steps block MOVE 4 + the registry visual's Zone C + mnemonics[3]

kypExtensions.summary: The statistical-vs-clinical significance layer: chance-language vs patients-language ('statistical significance says the result is unlikely to be chance; clinical significance says it matters for patients'), the sample-size-drives-the-first/effect-size-drives-the-second asymmetry, and the exam twist that re-dresses the printed 1 mg/dL blood-sugar example (big n makes small differences significant, not important).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the three definition sentences and the example; the two-language split, the n-vs-effect-size asymmetry, and the exam-twist packaging are KYP's design.
